To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

not-selfies, such as images of everyday objects, are a recognizable genre of self-representational visual communication in social media, and that the genre of self representation is not limited to the selfie.

selfies are not the only form of self-representation in contemporary social media; that selfies should not be reified as the natural or inevitable outcome of the social media context; and that the genre of selfrepresentation in social media is not necessarily about the body or the face, but is rather about the representation of selfhood.
not-selfies are a recognizable genre of visual self-representation that can be used to understand the ways in which people use visual media to represent themselves in social media.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the relationship between the self and its representation in digital media.
the ways that people make and share images of objects and animals in order to represent themselves.
the question of what counts as a self-representation, and what the implications of this are for understanding self-representation in the context of digital media.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
not-selfies are self-representation.
the selfie is not the only way to represent the self in digital communication.
not-selfies are a type of self-representation that does not feature the likeness of the person posting it.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
not all self-representation in the digital sphere involves the body, and that the body need not be central to the genre of self.
we argue that the selfie, as a form of self-representation, is best understood as a recognizable, emergent genre, and that the genre of the selfie is not synonymous with self-representation.
not-selfies can be considered as a genre of self-representative practices that do not feature a face.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the visual practices of self-representation in contemporary social media should not be reduced to a singular form, but rather understood as a diverse, evolving genre that is constantly being remade by its participants.
selfies and not-selfies are not opposites, but instead are part of the same genre of self-representational communication.
self-representation can be performed without the use of faces or bodies, and that the genre of self-portraiture is more varied than is often acknowledged.
